claims.text: Native connectors are purpose-built per application and call source APIs directly.
claims.excerpt: Purpose-built for specific applications (for example, Slack, Salesforce, Google Drive). They call source APIs directly

claims.text: Custom connectors push documents, metadata, and permissions via the Indexing API.
claims.excerpt: Custom connectors leverage Glean's indexing API to push documents, metadata, and permissions into the Glean platform.

claims.text: One shared queue: one backlog can delay another.
claims.excerpt: Documents, permissions, people data, and user activity all flow through the same backend queueing and indexing system at a high level, so one type of backlog can affect another.

claims.text: Connector function 1: data fetching, including the permissions map.
claims.excerpt: Data fetching: Connectors fetch data from connected applications and store the information in Glean's system.

claims.text: No runtime or hosting constraints.
claims.excerpt: Glean places no constraints on where a custom connector runs

claims.text: Connector function 2: content and permission parsing.
claims.excerpt: Content parsing: Connectors parse item content (for example, title, body, comments, media) and permissions

claims.text: Processing checks identity and permission dependencies before results show.
claims.excerpt: Verifies identities and access data. Waits for required dependencies.

claims.text: Processing expands derived groups and memberships.
claims.excerpt: Glean expands derived groups and memberships. This step associates u

claims.text: The Enterprise Graph is layered on the index and identity/permission structures.
claims.excerpt: connectors populate the index and associated identity and permission structures; the graph interpretation layers on structure and signals derived from that data.

claims.text: The runtime chooses index, live, or hybrid paths per request.
claims.excerpt: Choose data paths: Prefer index, live retrieval, or hybrid, per connector capabilities and query needs.

claims.text: RAG passes retrieved, permission-filtered snippets to the model.
claims.excerpt: Retrieved snippets are passed to the language model to condition the answer on your data.

claims.text: Indexing is asynchronous.
claims.excerpt: Indexing is asynchronous, so the document can take a few minutes to appear in search.

claims.text: Indexing can take around 15–20 minutes (varies).
claims.excerpt: Note that it takes around 15-20 minutes for the documents to be indexed and appear on your Glean UI.

claims.text: UPLOAD COMPLETED is acceptance, not searchability.
claims.excerpt: UPLOAD COMPLETED only means the API accepted your upload. It doesn't mean users are indexed and searchable.

claims.text: Documents are searchable after processingHistory passes bulkUploadHistory.
claims.excerpt: After documents are uploaded, they will be queued for processing. New documents will be available in search results when the processingHistory timestamp is after the bulkUploadHistory.

claims.text: The datasource must be enabled for search.
claims.excerpt: For the indexed document to show up in Glean UI, the datasource must be enabled for search.

claims.text: Search as the user is ground truth.
claims.excerpt: the search result is the ground truth, not the upload response.

claims.text: Accepted is not searchable.
claims.excerpt: Indexing is asynchronous - an accepted upload is not yet a searchable document.

claims.text: Worst case latency can exceed 24 hours.
claims.excerpt: Worst case: several hours to 24+ hours

claims.text: ACLs fail without pushed identities.
claims.excerpt: a correct-looking ACL is still wrong if the identities it names were never pushed.

claims.text: Unknown groups match nobody.
claims.excerpt: An ACL naming a group Glean has never heard of matches nobody.

claims.text: Bulk indexing replaces the datasource; omitted documents are deleted.
claims.excerpt: Bulk indexing fully replaces the entire list of documents stored in Glean. After a successful bulk upload, all documents that were not a part of the most recent upload are deleted asynchronously.

claims.text: /indexdocuments is for incremental updates.
claims.excerpt: /indexdocuments: This endpoint is intended for incremental updates.

claims.text: One unique uploadId per upload session.
claims.excerpt: You need to have a unique uploadId for all the paginated requests you send for an upload.

claims.text: No concurrent bulk uploads.
claims.excerpt: Concurrent uploads are not allowed ie. you cannot start a new upload before the previous upload is finished.

claims.text: After a failed upload, forceRestartUpload is required.
claims.excerpt: Not specifying this bit in case of an unsuccessful previous upload will fail the request.

claims.text: Full = replacement; incremental = additive.
claims.excerpt: A full crawl calls PushUploader.bulk_index_documents() for replacement and stale cleanup. An incremental crawl calls additive index_documents().

claims.text: Stale deletion pauses 7 days above 20%.
claims.excerpt: we have a deletion check in place which pauses the deletion of stale documents for 7 days if the percentage of docs being deleted exceeds 20%.

claims.text: Use /processalldocuments for immediate deletions.
claims.excerpt: If you wish for deletions to take effect immediately, use /processalldocuments endpoint.

claims.text: /processalldocuments: once every 3 hours per datasource.
claims.excerpt: /processalldocuments1 request every 3 hours per data source

claims.text: Never let a partial fetch complete as a full crawl.
claims.excerpt: Never let a partial or failed fetch finish as a successful full crawl.

claims.text: An empty full crawl clears the datasource.
claims.excerpt: A successful empty full crawl sends one complete empty bulk page so all previously indexed documents are reconciled as stale.

claims.text: Beta users still need document permissions.
claims.excerpt: For a document to be visible to beta users, they must also have appropriate permissions to view it.

claims.text: Choose the permissions model at setup.
claims.excerpt: Permissions model - whether documents are permission-aware (per-user ACLs pushed with each document) or visible to everyone in the org.

claims.text: Index users before referencing them.
claims.excerpt: When using non-anonymous permissions, users need to be indexed before being referenced.

claims.text: Index a group before its memberships.
claims.excerpt: groupName: A group with this particular groupName must be indexed before indexing memberships for it.

claims.text: Permissions and memberships process asynchronously.
claims.excerpt: Permissions and memberships are processed asynchronously

claims.text: The source may enforce access again at click time.
claims.excerpt: Opening a result usually sends the user to the source system, which may enforce access again at click time.

claims.text: allowAnonymousAccess exposes the document to every signed-in user.
claims.excerpt: allowAnonymousAccessIf set to true, anyone who is signed into Glean can view search results for the document

claims.text: allowAllDatasourceUsersAccess requires the user to be indexed as a datasource user.
claims.excerpt: allowAllDatasourceUsersAccess is true and user has been indexed as a user of the connector

claims.text: Indexing a user grants no document access.
claims.excerpt: Note that this does not give permissions to the users to search for the document

claims.text: Never allow-all 'for now'.
claims.excerpt: Never index sensitive content with an allow-all ACL "for now."

claims.text: Four-step missing-document diagnosis.
claims.excerpt: Most "the connector is broken" reports are really one of four things

claims.text: 'Appears then disappears' means stale deletion.
claims.excerpt: Appears, then disappears

claims.text: /processalldocuments reprocesses without a new upload.
claims.excerpt: This re-indexes all previously uploaded documents without requiring a new upload.

claims.text: Items over 64 MB index metadata and permissions only.
claims.excerpt: If the size is GREATER than 64 MB, the crawler WILL NOT download the item contents and will only download the metadata and permissions information for indexing.

claims.text: Metadata-only results cannot ground Assistant.
claims.excerpt: Can't be used for GenAI Glean Assistant will not be able to summarize the content

claims.text: Indexable text is truncated at 16.875 MB.
claims.excerpt: If the content is greater than 16.875 MB, then the first 16.875 MB of content will be stored and fed to the indexer.

claims.text: Apply the size limits to custom connectors too.
claims.excerpt: This speaks to Native Connector size limits, but should also be followed for Indexing documents into a Custom Connector

claims.text: Validate coverage and permissions in Search first.
claims.excerpt: Search is often the first place admins validate connector behavior (coverage and permissions) before relying on Chat, Assistant, or Agents.

claims.text: Native full re-crawl every 4 weeks as a catch-all.
claims.excerpt: Glean conducts a full re-crawl of the entire datasource every 4 weeks. This is technically not needed, but is done as a default "catch-all".

claims.text: Test datasources have ranking signals off.
claims.excerpt: All ranking signals are turned off from a test datasource.

claims.text: Counts prove nothing about permissions.
claims.excerpt: Counting indexed documents proves nothing about permissions.
